newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa July new car sales rise 2.1 pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa July new car sales rise 2.1 pct y/y.

text.p: New car sales rose 2.1 percent year-on-year and 9.1 percent month-on-month, the National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa (Naamsa) said on Tuesday.

"The improvement in new car sales manifest during June, 1997 continued during the month of July and at 21,994 units for the month registered a modest improvement of 454 units," the association said in a statement.
Following a 21.2 percent fall in May, new car sales rose 4.3 percent year-on-year in June.
The new car market had also continued to benefit from various special incentive offers as well as continuing interest in recently introduced models, it said.

Naamsa noted that the resilience in the new car market and an improvement in light commercial vehicle and medium commercial vehicle sales suggested the South African economy was experiencing a modest slowdown rather than heading for a recession.

It added, however, that against the background of continued high real interest rates, consumer indebtedness and a subdued economic environment -- it continued to forecast difficult trading conditions in the various sectors over the remainder of the year.

Toyota 10,401, Samcor 5,864, Delta 5,680, Volkswagen 5,526, Nissan 2,881, Mercedes-Benz 2,721, BMW 1,016, Daewoo 660, Land Rover SA 292, Chrysler 143, Iveco 74, MAN 51, Tyco 43, Freightliner 34, Scania 21, ERF 10, Subaru 10, AAD 5.
